body.title: Academic Intelligence Addendum — ENEB / Unimarconi international credential equivalency (owner, 26 Oct 2026)
Nuffic — Italian qualification guidance: Master universitario di primo livello (TO BE RETRIEVED AND ARCHIVED)

body.excerptText: An Italian Master universitario di primo livello must not automatically be classified as below master's level for international credential-evaluation purposes. Nuffic's official Italian qualification guidance normally compares this qualification to a Dutch professional master's (HBO), and sometimes to a research-university master's (WO), depending on the program. Positive U.S. WES degree-equivalency-tool results have also been reported for the general Italian Master Universitario category, although a completed, authenticated WES U.S. report for the exact ENEB–Unimarconi pathway has not yet been established. Absence of Italian doctoral-access rights does not establish absence of master's-level equivalency abroad.

body.statement: An Italian Master universitario di primo livello must not automatically be classified as below master's level for international credential evaluation. Equivalency is a credible, evidence-supported possibility, not a guaranteed outcome.
body.cohortApplicability: All cohorts; does not alter ENEB or Unimarconi academic rules

body.statement: Nuffic's Italian qualification guidance normally compares the Master universitario di primo livello to a Dutch professional (HBO) master's, and sometimes to a research-university (WO) master's, depending on the programme.

Positive WES U.S. degree-equivalency-tool results have been reported for the general Italian Master universitario category. These are preliminary tool results, not evaluation reports, and say nothing specific about the ENEB–Unimarconi pathway. WES Canada outcomes are a separate matter.

As of 26 Oct 2026 no completed, authenticated WES U.S. evaluation report has been established for an actual graduate awarded the first-level Unimarconi master's through ENEB. Obtaining one is the priority action.
Absence of Italian doctoral-access rights does not establish absence of master's-level equivalency abroad.
